entry.title: How LLM AI Agents Are Reshaping Software Engineering

link.title: How LLM AI Agents Are Reshaping Software Engineering

entry.content:
Introduction

LLM AI agents are becoming a new layer in software engineering. They don’t just autocomplete code — they plan, use tools, and iterate.

From Copilot to Agent

Early code completion was reactive: suggest the next line. Agents are proactive: take a goal, decompose it, and execute.

The MCP Protocol

Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how agents talk to tools. Once you have an MCP server, any agent that supports MCP can use it.

What’s Next

We’re moving from “AI that helps you code” to “AI that ships features.” The bottleneck is shifting from writing code to designing good agent workflows.
entry.summary: A practical look at how LLM-powered agents change the way we build and ship software.

entry.title: Lessons from Training Multimodal Foundation Models

link.title: Lessons from Training Multimodal Foundation Models

entry.content:
Why Pre-training Matters

The quality of your foundation model determines the ceiling of every downstream task. Garbage in, garbage out — at a billion-parameter scale.

Data Quality > Data Quantity

We spent 60% of our time on data curation. De-duplication, NSFW filtering, OCR cleanup, and language balancing mattered more than adding more raw images.

Compute Tricks

  • Gradient checkpointing for memory-bound layers
  • Flash attention for long sequences
  • Mixed precision (bf16) for stability

What Didn’t Work

Trying to fine-tune a 70B model on a single node. Just use LoRA.
entry.summary: What I learned from two years of pre-training large multimodal models at scale.
